mainText: Good morning, Landon. Here's your brief for Thursday, November 26, 2026. Happy Thanksgiving. Let's start with the markets. Stocks clawed back most of a steep early slide on Wednesday. The S&P 500 slipped 0.3 percent to 7,182, after falling as much as 3.2 percent during the day. The Nasdaq fell 0.6 percent to 23,585, while the Dow gained 0.3 percent to 50,182. AI stocks led the morning selloff before recovering, with Nvidia ending down nearly 4 percent, and a hot inflation report plus new tariff plans added to the pressure. Even so, all three indexes are up roughly 4 percent for the holiday shortened week. Treasury yields fell, with the 10 year near 4.85 percent. On the Fed, the central bank's preferred inflation gauge heated up. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.8 percent from a year earlier in October, in line with forecasts, and core prices, which exclude food and energy, rose 3.3 percent, a bit above expectations. Third quarter economic growth was also revised higher. Futures markets now put the odds of a quarter point rate hike at the December meeting at roughly 97 percent. The Fed's Beige Book reported growth in most regions, with prices still rising moderately. Next, the Trump administration proposed a new round of tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union, Japan, and India. The plan uses Section 301 trade law and would add 20 percent on Chinese goods, with most other partners expected to face rates between 10 and 18 percent. Next, HP shares jumped about 10 percent after the PC and printer maker beat fourth quarter forecasts, with revenue of 16 billion dollars, up more than 9 percent from a year ago. The company also raised its dividend, though it gave a cautious outlook for 2027. Next, Deere missed quarterly profit estimates on weakness in its large farm equipment business and issued a softer than expected forecast for next year, though its stock finished the day higher. And finally, oil prices climbed after Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery. Brent crude rose about 3.5 percent to roughly 94 dollars a barrel. On the calendar today, US stock and bond markets are closed for Thanksgiving, so there are no major earnings or economic releases. Trading resumes Friday with an early stock market close at 1 p.m. Eastern. Here's your fun fact. In a physics lab at Oxford University, a small bell has been ringing almost nonstop since 1840, powered by the same pair of batteries. It has rung an estimated 10 billion times, but it sits behind two layers of glass, so you can barely hear it. And because opening the batteries would end the experiment, scientists still are not sure exactly what they are made of. Have a great day.
